newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Tarapore confident of rupee convertibility.
newsitem.headline: India's Tarapore confident of rupee convertibility.

text.p: India has attained relative macroeconomic strength and can move confidently towards capital account convertibility (CAC) of the rupee, the chairman of the central bank committee planning the move said on Friday.

"Our monetary policies have been relatively sound over the last several years. We can now move towards capital account convertibility of the rupee with relative ease," S.S. Tarapore, chairman of the Reserve Bank of India's Committee on CAC said.
The committee headed by Tarapore, a former deputy governor of the central bank, recently recommended a three-phase strategy for making the rupee convertible on capital account by 2000.

Addressing a seminar organised by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry, titled "Towards CAC: 2000 AD", he said the arguments that the economy should attain a certain growth rate before CAC was implemented were wrong.

"Growth cannot be a precondition to CAC, growth is the end result of CAC. The country will get access to cheaper funds, higher yield on savings, and the prices of commodities and services will align with international prices," he said.

On the issue of the flight of capital, he said that these fears were misplaced. "After CAC, India will attract more capital rather that witness a flight of capital. The danger would be capital inflow rather than its flight," he said.

But, Tarapore warned that the punishment for wrong macroeconomic policies would be swift, once CAC was implemented. Flight of capital would register clearly in the exchange rate, reflecting a lack of confidence in policies, he said.
